basic_information.official_title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A LEVEL I GENERAL HOSPITAL IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF MALUSO, PROVINCE OF BASILAN, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates a 25-bed Level I general hospital in Maluso, Basilan, on the same terms as the Tipo-Tipo hospital passed the same day — including a tested, monitored path to provincial ownership.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: To put a general hospital in the municipality, and to build a path toward provincial management rather than permanent regional control.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: A hospital is established under the regional health ministry, which funds construction and initial running. Management transfers to the Provincial Government of Basilan when the province asks and the ministry agrees, or a five-yearly assessment finds it capable — with a joint transition plan, a one-year timetable, and parliamentary monitoring.
who_will_be_affected: Residents of Maluso and surrounding Basilan
The Provincial Government of Basilan, the intended eventual manager
Parliament, which monitors the transition plan and receives annual reports on continuing support
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2025 — 15 days after publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. A 25-bed Level I hospital for Maluso, built and run by the region at first, then handed to Basilan province on a tested trigger with a one-year handover and reports to Parliament.
in_practice: A Level I general hospital with 25-bed capacity in Maluso, Basilan
Under the administrative supervision and operational control of the Ministry of Health, which funds construction, infrastructure, equipment and initial maintenance and personnel costs
Implementing rules within 90 days of effectivity
The Chief of Hospital submits an annual development plan prepared with the Basilan Integrated Provincial Health Office, which governs personnel, capital outlays, budget and any future expansion
Transfer to the Provincial Government on a formal provincial request with MOH concurrence, or a favourable MOH assessment conducted every 5 years
A joint transition plan phases the turnover of responsibilities, personnel, assets and systems within 1 year of the transfer order
The transition plan goes to Parliament through the Committee on Health for information and monitoring
After transfer, the region continues technical support and, when necessary, financial support — with an annual report to Parliament

for_specific_groups.Residents of Maluso: A Level I general hospital in the municipality, funded and built by the region.
for_specific_groups.The Provincial Government of Basilan: You can request the transfer, but it needs MOH concurrence — or wait for the five-yearly assessment.
for_specific_groups.Anyone worried about devolution leaving: Section 6, the continuity provision, keeps regional technical and financial support in place after transfer, including salary augmentation and medical supplies.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since 2025; construction and the eventual handover follow their own timetables.
what_you_can_do: Ask the Committee on Health for the transition plan
Ask for the MOH's annual report on continuing technical and financial support
Ask for the hospital's annual development plan
watch_out_for: No construction completion deadline — the one-year timetable applies to the handover, not the building.
The province cannot take over unilaterally; MOH concurrence or a favourable assessment is required.
The MOH's annual reporting duty continues only while it is actually providing support.

key_terms_explained.Operational control: Day-to-day authority over how the hospital runs, held by the regional health ministry until transfer.
key_terms_explained.Continuity provision: The clause keeping regional support in place after the handover.
key_terms_explained.IPHO: Integrated Provincial Health Office, which co-prepares the annual development plan.

everyday_scenarios: A patient in Maluso gains a Level I general hospital in the municipality rather than travelling for basic hospital care.
Basilan's provincial government wants to run the hospital. It can formally request the transfer, but the health ministry must concur — or the province can wait for the five-yearly assessment.
After the handover the province cannot cover salaries 1 month. Section 6 lets the region temporarily augment operational requirements, and requires it to report that support to Parliament annually.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Establishes a Level I general hospital with 25-bed capacity in the Municipality of Maluso, Province of Basilan, to be known as the Maluso General Hospital (MGH).

Section 2 — The hospital is under the administrative supervision and operational control of the Ministry of Health, which determines and approves its organisational structure, formulates guidelines for its operation as a Level I hospital, and ensures funding for construction of the building and other complementary infrastructure, facilities and medical equipment, as well as initial maintenance and personnel costs pending full transfer of management under Sections 5 and 6. Implementing rules are due within 90 days of effectivity.

Section 3 — The Chief of Hospital, in consultation and coordination with the Basilan Integrated Provincial Health Office, submits to the MOH an annual development plan reflecting the hospital's developmental goals. Medical personnel, capital outlays and budgetary needs are based on that plan, and any future increase in bed capacity or upgrading of services must be consistent with it.
Section 4 — All relevant provisions of Republic Act 11223, the Universal Health Care Act, are integrated into the hospital's operational system.

Section 5 — Full management and control transfers from the Bangsamoro Government to the Provincial Government of Basilan on whichever comes first: a formal request from the Provincial Government with the concurrence of the MOH confirming readiness and institutional capacity; or a favourable assessment by the MOH, conducted every 5 years under its prescribed guidelines, determining that the Provincial Government has sufficient administrative, technical and financial capability to operate the hospital independently. The MOH then issues a formal order of transfer, effective on completion of a joint transition plan outlining the phased turnover of responsibilities, personnel, assets and systems, with a clear timetable not exceeding 1 year. The transition plan is submitted to the Bangsamoro Parliament, through the Committee on Health, for information and monitoring.

Section 6 — Continuity provision: notwithstanding the transfer, the Bangsamoro Government through the MOH shall continue to provide technical support and, when necessary, financial support. Financial support means temporary augmentation of operational requirements the Provincial Government cannot provide, including personnel salaries, essential medical supplies and equipment maintenance; technical support includes capacity building, policy guidance, health systems monitoring and quality assurance. The MOH shall submit an annual report to Parliament, through the Committee on Health and the Committee on Finance, Budget and Management, detailing the nature, scope and impact of that support, continuing only for the duration of the support.
Section 7 — An initial ₱50,000,000 is charged against the 2025 General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro, with continued operation and maintenance thereafter in the annual appropriations.
Section 10 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM.

citizen_questions.a: The regional Ministry of Health at first, with administrative supervision and operational control and responsibility for funding construction. Management then transfers to the Provincial Government of Basilan.

citizen_questions.q: When does the province take over?
citizen_questions.a: On whichever comes first: a formal provincial request with the health ministry's concurrence, or a favourable ministry assessment — conducted every 5 years — that the province can operate the hospital independently.

A joint transition plan must set a timetable not exceeding 1 year from the transfer order, covering responsibilities, personnel, assets and systems, and goes to Parliament's Committee on Health for monitoring.

citizen_questions.q: What if the province cannot cope after taking over?
citizen_questions.a: Section 6 keeps the region providing technical support and, when necessary, financial support — including temporary help with salaries, essential medical supplies and equipment maintenance — with an annual report to Parliament.

citizen_questions.q: Is this the same as the Tipo-Tipo hospital act?
citizen_questions.a: Substantially yes. BAA 78 and this act were passed and approved on the same days for the same province and carry the same devolution scheme, differing mainly in the municipality and the section heading of the continuity clause.
